page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor. It features 24 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not included, meaning the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression performing in the bottom 10%. However, the 24 dedicated cores deliver average multi-core performance, with Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is also average, reaching 90.83 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is its reliance on older Intel Broadwell architecture, which limits single-threaded execution speed but offers stable, dedicated multi-core capacity. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this hardware profile provides a predictable resource density for multi-threaded workloads without the premium cost of newer-generation architectures. It is suitable for general-purpose workloads that benefit from parallel processing, such as static web serving, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded application hosting, while being less optimal for single-threaded tasks or memory-intensive databases.
